diseases.name: Infective endocarditis
diseases.tool: Modified Duke criteria are used by specialists; apply separately.

diseases.name: HIV infection / opportunistic infection
diseases.inv: HIV test with counselling per national programme (NACO), CD4 count.

diseases.name: Visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar)
diseases.inv: rK39 rapid test, CBC, bone marrow/splenic aspirate by specialist.

diseases.name: Leptospirosis
diseases.alt: Dengue, malaria, viral hepatitis, scrub typhus

diseases.name: Scrub typhus / rickettsial infection
diseases.inv: Scrub typhus IgM ELISA; look for eschar.

diseases.name: Reactive lymphadenitis
diseases.inv: Treat source; review if not settling.

diseases.name: Tuberculous lymphadenitis
diseases.inv: FNAC with AFB stain/CBNAAT, chest X-ray.

diseases.name: Lymphoma / metastatic lymph nodes
diseases.inv: Excision biopsy of node, CBC, imaging; specialist care.

diseases.name: Necrotising soft-tissue infection
diseases.inv: Emergency surgical review; do not delay; CBC, lactate, imaging only if it does not delay care.

diseases.name: Tetanus
diseases.alt: Dental infection, drug-induced dystonia, strychnine poisoning

diseases.name: Local wound infection
diseases.inv: Clinical; swab if purulent; check tetanus immunisation.

diseases.name: Recurrent aphthous ulcers
diseases.inv: Clinical; check for iron, B12, folate deficiency or inflammatory bowel disease.

diseases.name: Oral cancer / premalignant lesion
diseases.inv: Urgent biopsy and specialist (ENT/oral surgery) review.
diseases.alt: Aphthous ulcer, traumatic ulcer, TB, candidiasis

diseases.name: Rabies exposure (needs post-exposure prophylaxis assessment)
diseases.inv: Wash wound for 15 minutes with soap and water; assess category and start PEP per WHO/national guidelines, tetanus prophylaxis.
diseases.alt: Non-rabid animal exposure, bacterial wound infection

diseases.name: Snakebite envenoming
diseases.inv: 20-minute whole blood clotting test, urgent antivenom assessment; keep limb still.

flags.text: Animal bite/scratch/lick: rabies post-exposure prophylaxis assessment is urgent; wash wound now
Snakebite with neurotoxic or bleeding signs: emergency; immobilise limb and go to hospital for antivenom assessment
Rapidly spreading painful skin infection with systemic illness: possible necrotising infection, emergency
Stiff jaw or muscle spasms with a wound: possible tetanus, emergency
